content:
Dear Verdane Care team,

I’m applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience squad. I’m a full-stack developer with 12 years of professional experience, strongest in React and TypeScript, and with hands-on experience building Node.js services and working with PostgreSQL. Verdane Care’s focus on patient-facing tools, accessible design and privacy by default makes this role especially compelling.

In my current role at Älvgrind Fintech, I build onboarding features using React, TypeScript, NestJS and PostgreSQL. I built a BankID identity-verification flow that was A/B tested before rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%. I also implemented a secure ID-document upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, virus scanning in Lambda and scan-status handling through SQS. These projects have given me practical experience building end-to-end features where usability and careful handling of sensitive information matter.

I’ve also contributed to an incremental migration of an onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, and maintained an Apollo Server BFF. Earlier, as project tech lead in a two-developer team, I built most of a React Native ferry-ticket app, which now has around 50,000 downloads. I’d be glad to bring this mix of frontend strength, backend delivery and hands-on product experience to Verdane Care’s patient-facing work.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Patient Experience squad.

Best regards,
Oskar

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, well structured, and tailored to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience role. It presents strong evidence through concrete outcomes, including the 61% to 74% onboarding conversion increase and the approximately 50,000 mobile-app downloads. The examples also demonstrate end-to-end delivery, frontend strength, backend experience, and responsible handling of sensitive information. The main weakness is completeness: several requirements that the candidate may be able to support are not surfaced, particularly security fundamentals, accessibility, testing, Git workflows, and willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements. These omissions limit the letter’s persuasive value, although they do not indicate that the candidate lacks those capabilities.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings-free prose, conventional punctuation, readable paragraphs, and relevant exact terms such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, S3, Lambda, SQS, Express, and A/B tested. There are no tables, graphics, unusual symbols, or formatting elements likely to impair parsing. AI screening probability is good when the associated CV is considered because the CV contains the strongest technical keyword coverage. For the cover letter alone, screening coverage is moderate rather than excellent because it does not explicitly include terms from the advertisement such as accessibility, automated testing, Git-based workflows, authentication, or privacy requirements.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the core full-stack stack: the document clearly shows substantially more than two years of React and TypeScript experience, Node.js backend work, SQL/PostgreSQL, AWS familiarity, and analytics/A/B testing. The identity-verification and secure-document-upload examples are relevant to Verdane Care’s privacy-by-default focus, although the letter appropriately does not claim healthcare experience. The ferry-ticket application supports product ownership, mobile usability, and technical leadership. The document does not show semantic HTML, responsive layouts, web accessibility, automated unit/integration/end-to-end testing, Git workflows, OWASP Top 10 awareness, German or Croatian, Next.js/server-side rendering, Docker, design systems, or Storybook. The candidate material also does not establish healthcare experience or explicit willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements. These are candidate-evidence gaps or unsupported areas, not defects that should be invented through rewriting.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the second paragraph, make the security relevance more explicit without claiming unsupported OWASP expertise. Replace the sentence beginning "These projects have given me practical experience" with: "These projects gave me practical experience with authentication, secure file handling, virus scanning, and careful handling of sensitive customer information—experience that aligns with Verdane Care’s privacy-by-default approach." This is supported by the BankID identity-verification flow and the S3 presigned-upload, ClamAV, Lambda, and SQS implementation described in the associated CV.

2. In the third paragraph, connect the candidate’s existing A/B-testing evidence more directly to the product-development responsibilities in the advertisement. After the sentence ending "74%," add: "I also value validating product changes with real usage data rather than relying only on assumptions." Keep this grounded in the documented A/B test and do not claim experience with usability sessions unless it can be verified.

3. In the closing paragraph, replace "this mix of frontend strength, backend delivery and hands-on product experience" with "this mix of frontend strength in React and TypeScript, Node.js/NestJS backend delivery, PostgreSQL experience, and hands-on product experience." This adds exact job-ad and ATS terminology already supported by the candidate’s material while making the fit for the Patient Experience squad more explicit.
